parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Choose a company you can describe honestly
parts.body:
The capstone begins with an enterprise whose choices can be explained. A real public company gives you filings and product information, but internal budgets, data rights, and maturity may remain unknown. A realistic invented company lets you control those details, provided every invented fact is labeled. Pick one business unit or operating process to keep the plan testable.

Write a one-page case brief: how the company earns revenue, customers and workers affected, strategic priorities, current workflow, technology estate, data sources and rights, operating regions, risk tolerance, and AI capability. Separate sourced facts, reasonable assumptions, and open questions. The Stanford AI Index can inform the wider context, but industry averages do not establish this company's baseline.

Choose a measurable business tension. 'Become an AI leader' gives you no basis for tradeoffs. 'Reduce avoidable claims handling time without raising reopened cases' identifies a workflow, outcome, and countermeasure. The case should permit at least one worthwhile use you choose to postpone.

example.title: Completed enterprise brief
example.body: Fictional Northlake Mutual earns premiums from property insurance and pays covered claims. Scope: internal first drafts of Canadian home claims for 40 adjusters; a human checks every draft and decides coverage. Objective: reduce median drafting time from an assumed 18 minutes to 14 without increasing reopened claims above an assumed 5%. Operating regions: Canada for the pilot; an EU subsidiary is excluded. Current estate: a legacy claims system, a document store with unverified record permissions, and no deployed generative AI. Constraints: sensitive claim narratives, uncertain retrieval rights, limited integration staff. The business owner is the claims VP. All volumes, baselines, systems, and maturity details are case assumptions, not findings about a real insurer.

exercise.title: Write the case brief
exercise.body: Choose real or hypothetical. State one business objective, eligible workflow, affected people, regions, three constraints, a baseline measure, and a countermeasure. Label each case fact sourced, assumed, or unknown.

sources: NIST AI RMF Playbook: Map context

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Build the assumption register
parts.body:
An assumption register prevents a clean narrative from passing as evidence. Give each entry a proposition, source or reason, confidence, impact if wrong, validation owner, due date, and decision affected. Rank assumptions by how strongly they could change your recommendation, not by how easy they are to check.

For the insurer case, access rights to historical claims, baseline handling time, and the vendor's data terms could all overturn the roadmap. An analyst can measure handling time in a sample. Privacy counsel and the data owner must assess whether the intended use of claim text is permitted. Procurement and security can inspect vendor terms and controls. Until then, show the pilot as conditional.

Keep hypotheses separate from commitments. A claimed 20% efficiency gain belongs in a scenario, not the benefits-realized column. Write what you would do if a pivotal assumption fails: use de-identified examples, narrow the task to internal drafting, choose a different vendor, or stop. The exercise rewards candor because an executive plan must survive discovery.

example.title: A short assumption register
example.body: Northlake Mutual, fictional: (1) 80% of draft cases have permissioned source records, low confidence, high impact; data owner samples 100 cases by week four and blocks real-data pilot funding if access fails. (2) Median draft time is 18 minutes, low confidence, high impact; claims operations times 50 current cases by week three. (3) Vendor retention can meet the company's proposed terms, unknown confidence, high impact; procurement, privacy, and security review the contract before any transfer. (4) Adjusters will use drafts in at least half of eligible cases, low confidence, medium impact; claims VP tests workflow with ten volunteers during discovery. Quantities are invented; the owners and gates show how the assumptions would be checked.

exercise.title: Find a plan-breaking assumption
exercise.body: List six assumptions. For each, record validation, owner, date, impact, and fallback. Circle the two that could reverse your first investment decision and place their tests early in the roadmap.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Map and Measure
OECD due diligence guidance for responsible AI

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Map jurisdiction and stakeholder boundaries
parts.body:
List the places where a system is provided or used, where affected people are located, and which personal or sensitive data enters the workflow. For EU activity, ask counsel to assess the organization's provider or deployer role, AI Act classification, applicable dates, and data protection duties. For Canada, identify the applicable federal or provincial privacy regime and the purpose and safeguards for processing. Do not infer one rule for every insurer or every AI use.

Name the stakeholders who can change the plan: claims leaders, adjusters, customers, data owners, CIO, CISO, privacy and legal teams, and finance. Put their concerns beside the planned decision. A worker may need an override and a way to report a bad draft; a customer may need a clear route to correct a claim record. These are design questions to resolve, not claims that a particular law always mandates the same interface.

Write down the authority map. The CAIO can coordinate evaluation and recommend priority, while the business executive owns the workflow outcome and control owners retain their authority. This boundary will matter later when a pilot fails a release condition.

example.title: A completed jurisdiction line
example.body: Northlake Mutual pilot: Canadian adjusters, Canadian home-claim records, internal draft assistance, human coverage decisions. Privacy lead determines the applicable Canadian federal or provincial regime and validates purpose, access, retention, and safeguards by week four; the claims VP decides whether to pilot after that review. The EU subsidiary and EU data are excluded. Any EU expansion requires an EU data-flow map, provider or deployer role and AI Act classification review, privacy review, language-specific evaluation, and approval by its operating owner. No legal conclusion is assumed.

exercise.title: Draw the boundary
exercise.body: For the first use case, create a table of region, affected person, data, proposed use, legal question, reviewer, decision owner, and release gate. Identify one seemingly small expansion that would require reassessment.

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Test whether the case supports decisions
parts.body:
Before designing the roadmap, check whether the case has enough evidence to compare use cases. You need a baseline for one outcome, a plausible unit of demand, a known decision owner, and a way to sample quality. If any is missing, make discovery the first funded phase with a bounded duration and cost.

A candidate should also show why another attractive use waits. In the insurer case, internal drafting might permit mandatory human review and a controlled sample. Automated claim denial would touch a more consequential decision and needs a different assessment, evidence standard, and authority. The choice reflects scope and evidence, not an assertion that one use is categorically lawful or unlawful.

Give a peer only the case brief and assumption register. Ask them to propose an investment. If they cannot identify the customer, baseline, geographic scope, and biggest unresolved dependency, rewrite the brief. If they confidently approve a full rollout, check whether you accidentally presented forecasts as observations.

example.title: A discovery decision from the case brief
example.body: Northlake Mutual's claims VP approves an illustrative six-week, CAD 60,000 discovery cap for the Canadian drafting case. By week three, operations measures 50 current cases; by week four, the data owner checks 100 records, while privacy and security assess the proposed data flow and vendor. By week six, the evaluation lead reports a supervised test against the 18-minute and 5% assumed baselines, revised with observed data. No production use or EU scope is authorized. If rights or vendor terms fail, the VP defers the pilot and funds a narrower data-remediation decision. The cap and baselines are fictional.

exercise.title: Run a case review
exercise.body: Ask a peer to name the first decision, two plan-breaking assumptions, and one deferred use. Revise the brief until those are evident without oral explanation. Keep the peer's objections for the executive defense.
